title: How does anxiety show up for you?
intro: Anxiety doesn't always look like panic attacks. Sometimes it shows up as overthinking, physical tension, racing thoughts, irritability, or feeling unable to relax. This check-in is designed to help you recognize how anxiety may currently be affecting your thoughts, body, emotions, and nervous system.

options.text: Full of racing thoughts and overthinking
Overwhelmed internally even if I seem calm outside
Uncomfortable whenever things become too quiet or still

questions.text: When stress shows up, I usually:

options.text: Feel anxiety physically in my body
Panic internally while trying to hold it together
Distract myself to avoid slowing down
My brain won't fully shut off
My nervous system is always scanning for stress

questions.text: People around me probably see me as:

options.text: Thoughtful or stuck in my head

questions.text: What do you need most right now?

a.description: You experience constant racing thoughts, mental spirals, and difficulty turning the brain off. Your mind works hard — sometimes too hard — and struggles to find quiet.

b.description: You are always scanning for problems, stress, or potential danger and struggle to fully relax. Your nervous system is stuck in high alert even when things are okay.

c.description: You carry anxiety physically through tension, discomfort, restlessness, or nervous system activation. Your body holds what your mind is processing.

d.description: You feel panic and overwhelm internally while appearing calm externally. You carry a lot quietly — more than most people around you realize.

e.description: You avoid slowing down because stillness feels uncomfortable or emotionally overwhelming. Staying busy keeps you from having to sit with difficult feelings.
